title: Arthur Selig Sr.'s band, Palm Court and the Rogers drummers
summary: Schiro lists sidemen at the country club, Palm Court and spotlight; talk of Wiffle and the Rogers drummers.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: And then I also played with Arthur Selig Sr. at the St. Bernard Country Club after the Haunted Giordino level. We had a nice set up there. We had Arthur Selig Sr. on bass and guitar. And with Roz Zimmerman on piano. And Pierre Cirio. And with Paul Dana and myself on saxes. Charlie DuPont and I too. He was the Bupin on trumpet. And sometimes we had, on the drums we had, the boy's name, he was Lester Gauze. And then the other man that was something for him sometime was Leo Addy. He died too. Yeah. And Arthur Selig Sr. at the famous door number. And then also played at the Palm Court which was across the street in the Silver Slip at the time. And he played with Joe Gailer. You ever heard of him? No I don't know. He played a nice piano. Coats. You know, good chords. He and Henry Carubo on drums. And a little. Was he sometime. Whiffle was his name. I think. It was in relation to Stormy Rogers or something. He played drums? Yeah. He was a private thing boy, private thing.
There was Emmett and there was Buck Rogers.
I think it was Emmett, yeah. There was some relation up here. He played fine drums too.
I remember who you were talking about again. I heard of him. I'll ask Raymond Burke about it. I think Raymond thought about him. Wiffle Rogers. Yeah, we used to call him Wiffle.
Which one was Stew Meat Rogers? Yeah, Stew Meat. He's a good one. Same guy? It's a Nipper's Buck. Yeah. It's either Buck or Nipper.
Yeah. Well, maybe I got a picture up in here. Yeah. Keep talking, I'll find a picture.

And then I also played at the spotlight across the street from the famous Dill. We used to make it down at half the night and tips there. Hmm. Yeah. See, there was another band I also played with. That was with Jill Clessie, Tweety, Francis Murray. And Louis Caravello on drums. He's now playing bass. He's working for the railroad. Sometimes he comes out of height and sits in with us. Sometimes on the drums, sometimes on the bass. At Lodgins, huh? Yeah, let's see.
Here's a picture of Raymond Rogers. Yes. That's the one they call Wiffle? No.
No. No, he was extra thin blood.
Yeah. Yeah. Well, Buck was the uncle of Nett. Yeah. Of Nett. Yeah. So he was old, about a few years, I think. Buck was old, about a few years. Uh huh. Buck was old, Nett.
